title: Cornet versus trumpet
summary: He traded trumpet for cornet to fit an old-style group and discusses tone; Kid Howard and Sidney De Paris use both instruments.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Now you play Cornet or trumpet? Cornet.

No. Oh, years ago, well, the first instrument I bought was a trumpet. And, uh, I played it quite some time. And, well, when I got to playing with the Last Straw, I was naturally being supposed to be an old jazz group. They use the old type of instrument, so I went and traded my, uh, trumpet in for a Cornet. The Cornet being the old type of instrument, it fits in with that, uh, with that set-up, see?
Can you tell any difference in the tone or anything?

Uh, I think, uh, well, from what I can understand, I think a Cornet is supposed to be more of a solo instrument. You see, uh, your trumpet, your trumpet, uh, might have a sweeter tone, higher pitch, but a Cornet, a Cornet's just a solo instrument. It's just a big brass instrument. It makes a lot of noise, see? It's supposed to be the lead instrument, and you, I guess you're supposed to hear this one louder than any other, huh?
Do you like, which tone do you like the best, really, if you had your choice?

Uh, how do you mean, uh, which, which tone? The trumpet or the clarinet? Oh, I like, I like, uh, I like the Cornet. I like the Cornet. So, you know, you take, uh, these fellows that play, you know, strictly the sweet dance music, uh, they would have to use trumpet. See, it's that, that type of instrument where the Cornet's, uh, more of a, what you'd say, uh, something that would be used in a brass band or a marching band or something of that type, see? He was a cornet.
It's funny, Kid Howard would have switched back to Cornet, too, you know?
Did he switch back? I know, uh, I have, uh, a recording horn by George Lewis, and on the, uh, jacket, on the album jacket, they show, uh, Kid Howard playing a trumpet. Yeah. He's got a trumpet.

But he's back on the Cornet, and you even see modern guys now going to the Cornet, like, I heard Melvin last year, uh, I think it was Friday night, uh, at, uh, the jazz room on Dolphin Street, you know? Yeah, at the corner. And, uh, he was playing Cornet.

Well, uh, I was, uh, fortunate enough to catch, uh, Wilbert DiPerry's group in New York. And, uh, Sidney DiPerry has both a trumpet and a Cornet. He hangs them both on his music stand. Now, whichever tune they play, the type of tune he plays, that, you know, that's the decided fact as to which instrument he will use. If they play the real old New Orleans, uh, Mark stuff, he takes his cornet. If he plays something, maybe more of a, uh, a dance tune, he'll use his trumpet.
